title: Calm Streak
statement: A weather station logs one temperature reading per hour. A stretch of consecutive hours is *calm* if every pair of neighboring readings in it differs by at most `k` degrees.
Given the readings and `k`, return the length of the longest calm stretch. A single reading on its own is a calm stretch of length 1, and an empty log has no stretch at all.

examples.explanation: 30, 31, 31, 29 changes by at most 2 from hour to hour.

hints: You only ever need to compare a reading with the one right before it.
Walk through the readings once, keeping the length of the calm stretch that ends at the current hour.
When a jump is bigger than k, the stretch ending here starts over at length 1. Keep the best length you've seen.
pitfalls: Forgetting the absolute value, so a big drop in temperature counts as calm.
Comparing each reading with the first one in the stretch instead of its neighbor.
Counting the differences between readings instead of the readings themselves, which is off by one.
interviewerNotes: Check whether they confirm that only neighboring readings are compared, not every pair in the stretch.
Ask about the empty log and a single reading.
Follow-up: if calm meant max minus min in the stretch is at most k, how would the solution change? Strong candidates reach for a sliding window with monotonic deques.
